en: A quivering lump of jelly that rolls through grass and dunes. It is harmless unless provoked, and leaves sticky jelly behind when it bursts.

A towering figure in an oversized black cloak that hides its hands and feet. Its head is an orange skull with red glowing eyes and a mouth full of fangs. It is the master of doom, and also of more doom.
An ordinary resident of a settlement, going about their day.
A creature made for game masters to try things on. It is strong, wears every piece of gear and knows every attack a bestia can learn. It never appears in the wild.
A plump brown rat that lives in the furrows at the edge of fields. It bolts at the first footstep, so approach it from downwind.
Roots up fields with its broad snout and charges whoever bothers it. Its thick hide shrugs off stones, but a sharp gust makes it stumble.
A long-eared hopper that comes out to graze at dusk. Tailors in every start town want its soft pelt.
Buries itself so only its leaves show, then screams when stepped on. Watch for grass that grows in odd tufts.
A fat green caterpillar that chews leaves all day. It spits sticky silk that slows the legs of anyone who bothers it.
A fly that swarms around anything that smells of fruit. Alone it is a nuisance; in a cloud it is a problem.
A chick that hatches in sun-baked sand and still wears half its eggshell. Its pecks are warm, so it fears water more than swords.
Scuttles sideways along the tideline and snaps at bare toes. Its shell turns blows from the front; strike it from the side.
A round frog whose belly swirl hypnotises flies. It croaks loudest just before rain.
A golden fish that leaps out of the water for no reason anyone can name. On land it only splashes, and it is very proud of it.
A white fox cub that dives head-first into snowdrifts to catch mice. Its fur keeps it warm in deep frost, but it pants in summer sun.
A proud penguin that slides on its belly faster than most can run. It guards the colony's ice holes and pecks anyone who comes close.
Hides under hot stones and stings whatever steps near. Carry an antidote before you lift a rock in the desert.
A cheeky monkey that snatches shiny things and flees into the canopy. Keep a hand on your purse under the trees.
A slow snail that leaves a toxic slime trail across the peat. Do not walk where the moss glistens.
A butterfly with wings like stained glass. The dust it sheds makes eyes heavy, so do not fight it in a clearing full of them.
A walking mushroom that puffs out spores when hit. Fire makes short work of it, and of the spores too.
A rock with arms that rolls downhill on purpose. It looks like any other stone until it gets up.
A pale flame that bobs over the marsh at night and leads travellers astray. Plain blows pass through it; magic does not.
Curls into a spiky ball when threatened and rolls at its attacker. Hit it before it curls up.
A raccoon that balances a leaf on its head and swears it is a disguise. It hoards mushrooms and trinkets in hollow logs.
A ragged hawk that dives on anything smaller than itself, and some things that are not. It strikes out of the sun, so look up on open ground.
Grazes in great herds that stamp the plains flat. Harm one calf and the whole herd turns on you.
Grey wolves that hunt in packs under the pines. They circle before they bite; keep your back to a tree.
Looks like a pine cone on a branch until it drops on your head. It throws cones that burst into splinters.
A huge bear that raids bee nests and sleeps it off in the sun. Wake it at your own risk; it is far quicker than it looks.
Leaps from ledge to ledge where no path exists. It charges from above and tries to knock climbers off the cliff.
Half woman, half vulture, all temper. Harpies nest on cliff tops and shriek to call the flock.
A shaggy yak whose wool never freezes. Nomads follow its herds, and its wool sells well in the warm south.
A snowman that came alive in a blizzard and never thawed. Fire melts its grin off fast, and it knows to keep its distance.
A walrus that dozes on ice floes in big groups. Mothers with pups attack anything that comes near.
A see-through jellyfish that washes up after storms. Its threads sting and numb the limbs, so do not wade in after a storm.
A starfish with a glowing core that spins across the sand at night. The core is a crafting gem, and it knows it.
Lies as still as a log in shallow water. River folk say: if a log has eyes, walk the other way.
A swollen toad with poison sacs in its cheeks. It puffs up before it spits; that is your moment to move.
A peat-soaked corpse that crawls out of the bog when the mist is thick. Holy light and fire send it back down.
Rolls balls of dung across the dunes and buries them with lost coins inside. Dig where it digs.
A wrapped corpse that guards tombs long after its masters turned to dust. Its loose bandages burn well.
A sand viper that moves sideways and leaves strange tracks on the dunes. Its venom slows the heart, so a cure is worth its weight in water.
A spotted scavenger whose laugh carries far. Where the cackling starts, something weak is about to die; make sure it is not you.
A lizard that soaks up sun on hot rocks until its scales glow. Hunt it in the cold morning, before it has warmed up.
A walking hill of stone, slow to anger and slower to stop. Wind cuts into its cracks; blades just ring.
A pup with an ember for a nose. Wild ones guard hot vents in packs; tamed ones make the best watchdogs alive.
A blob of living lava that oozes over cooling rock. It leaves a burning trail, so never follow it in light boots.
A turtle that sleeps in hot springs with only its nose above water. Startle it and it shoots a jet of scalding water.
A little horned trickster that smells of rotten eggs. It plays pranks on travellers by the vents, and some pranks explode.
A lion with a mane that glows like dawn, leading its pride over the savanna. Shadow creatures avoid its land, and so should you.
A mantis with sickle arms that waits motionless in tall grass. It is fast but light; heavy blows knock it flat.
A rooted flytrap that bites anything in reach. It cannot move, so fight it from afar.
A stag with ferns growing in its antlers. It is gentle, but in rutting season it fights anything with horns, and anything without.
Small dog-faced miners that dig for ore and fight over every scrap. Their camps are full of stolen tools.
A huge flightless bird that runs fastest in a thunderstorm. Riders dream of taming one; most only ever see its tail.
An old willow that drags its branches through the water and drowns what it catches. Fire is the only thing it fears.
A cactus that walks to new water at night. It fires needles when touched, and its flesh holds water for thirsty travellers.
A black lynx that hunts only in darkness and vanishes into its own shadow. Carry a light; it will not attack inside one.
A giant snake the colour of jungle vines. It drops from the canopy and squeezes; a friend nearby is the best cure.
A shaggy giant whose roar starts avalanches. It hurls blocks of ice, so never let it take the high ground.
A slender drake that sleeps in boiling pools and breathes steam. Its scales stay warm long after it dies.
Fish-folk with tridents who raid the coast at high tide. They flee to the sea when hurt, so finish the fight on the sand.
A whirl of dust and an old grudge drifting over cold dunes. Ordinary weapons pass through it; enchanted ones do not.
A huge brute that clubs first and thinks never. Its swings are wide; stay close and keep moving.
A water horse that waits by the shore, calm and saddled. Whoever climbs on is dragged into the lake.
A pale unicorn seen only on moonlit nights. It flees at the sight of drawn weapons; only a gentle master can tame it.
A silver-backed ape that beats its chest like thunder. It throws whole branches and fights harder when its troop is near.
A sea serpent that rises from the surf during storms. Fishers wait for calm weather for a reason.
A weeping ghost whose wail freezes the blood. Cover your ears and close in fast.
A many-headed swamp lizard that bites with each head in turn. Burn the stumps, or the heads grow back.
A white wyvern that nests in glacier cracks and breathes freezing wind. It must land to breathe again; that is when you strike.
A lizard of pure flame that swims through lava. Water hurts it badly; getting close enough to splash it is the hard part.
A sand serpent that hunts by feeling footsteps through the dunes. Stand still and it may pass you by.
A wyvern that rides the hot winds out of the canyons. Its screech knocks climbers off the walls.
A tangle of limbs from the other side of the Rift. It flickers between worlds; strike when it is solid.
Empty armour still holding the line it swore to hold before the Rift. It never retreats and never tires; holy blades break its oath.
An angel the corruption twisted into a mockery of itself. Its halo has turned black, and it hates light.
When enough blobs gather they merge into a quivering queen with a jelly crown. She splits off blobs when hurt, so clear the small ones fast.
A beetle with a shell of beaten gold that nests in buried treasure vaults. Magic slides off its shell; steel does not.
A tiger whose stripes burn like coals. The savanna burns where it hunts, and it waits for prey in the smoke.
Queen of a hive the size of a house. She never fights alone; a cloud of guards follows her.
Warlord of the forest clans, in armour made of trophies. His war horn calls every orc nearby.
A spirit of clear water who sings on still lakes at dawn. She is calm until the lake is fouled, then she floods the shore.
The ghost captain of a wrecked ship, still giving orders to a dead crew. He comes with the fog, and his crew comes with him.
A fox with nine flaming tails who jumps between old shrines. Each tail is a spell; count them as they go out.
The oldest tree in the forest, which walks only once in many years. Whole groves grow on its back, and it wakes angry when they are cut.
The great flame every lantern wisp comes from. Put out her wisps and she grows weak.
A buried king who rises when his tomb is disturbed. His curse follows whoever takes his gold.
A giant flower whose stench carries for miles. Its pollen poisons the air around it; fight upwind.
A dragon that sleeps in sulphur vents and breathes poison gas. Where the hot springs turn yellow, it is near.
A white stag with antlers of light, the old guardian of the forest. Shadow creatures cannot stand near it.
A giant wolf of ice whose howl brings blizzards. The wolf packs of the north follow it.
A huge bird that nests on peaks and calls lightning with its wings. Earth magic grounds it.
A mammoth older than the ice it walks on. It sleeps frozen for years and wakes up hungry.
A goat-headed demon with a huge scythe who preaches to the corrupted. Its sermons summon lesser demons.
A walking volcano that sleeps under the lava fields. When it wakes, the ground cracks and new vents open.
A green dragon that circles above the rain clouds and rarely lands. It only comes down when the jungle burns.
The king who ruled before the Rift and refused to die with his kingdom. He holds the corrupted land with an army of the dead.
A bird of living flame that rises from fresh lava once in a long while. It is reborn from its ashes, so the fight is never quite over.
The bones of an ancient dragon, raised by the corruption. It cannot be poisoned or frightened, but it can be broken.
A sea dragon as long as an island that surfaces only far out at sea. The waves it makes reach every coast.
A horned giant that walks the plains once in an age and leaves valleys in its tracks. The game is named after it; nobody has brought one down yet.
A pumpkin with a candle inside and a grin nobody carved. It only grows on the night the dead walk.
A present with a bow that hops through the snow at midwinter. Open it gently; sometimes it bites.
A hare with blossoms in its ears that hides painted eggs in spring meadows. Find its eggs and it may come to you.
It looks exactly like a blob. It is not a blob. Your sword passes right through it, which a real blob would never allow.
